question: What changed in Microsoft's filings, DCF math, and tape as of November 20, 2026, and what is our exact action?

epigraph.quote: Good underwriting separates business durability from entry timing, then right-sizes exposure before support breaks.
epigraph.author: Institutional Research Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT) remains an elite compounder ($92,279M Q1 FY27 sales +19% YoY, 49.7% OPM, +48% Azure, $677B RPO [5, 31]), earning COMPOUNDER_PASS with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health. Yet Pass 1 footnotes revealed heavier cash demands. Q1 PP&E ($39.4B), component outflows ($12.95B), and finance leases ($5.19B) consumed $57.5B of $58.0B CFO [31]. Microsoft then closed $25.0B in senior notes on November 4 [32], uncommenced leases hit $364.6B, and Q1 OpenAI sales reached $10.0B [31].

At $484.52 (20.11x forward P/E [26]), an exact 10-year DCF (9.1% WACC on a 5.04% 10-year yield, plus an FY27–28 CapEx hump) shows the market already prices in 13.75% revenue compounding. Our reconciled $540.00 Base fair value ($538.12 DCF / 22.5x FY28E EPS) offers +11.45% upside (a 10.27% discount to fair value) against -22.6% Bear risk ($375.00) and Bull $660.00. Because MSFT broke its 50-DMA ($519.84) into Stage 3 inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend, new capital stays on WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT ($462.00–$476.00 watch zone; 2.88:1 technical R:R; 0.0% live allocation). On the 12.4022 Schwab shares ($6,009.11 MV, 8.00% weight), we assign TRIM_OVERWEIGHT: sell 4.0 shares (~$1,938.08 into 100% USD Cash) to right-size to 8.4022 shares (5.42% weight) under an unconditional single-close or intraday $453.81 stop.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — Honest DCF Math & Active Risk Control
paragraphs: Reconciling our 10-year DCF removed inflated target anchors and revealed a narrow +11.45% Base cushion at $484.52. Trimming 4.0 overweight shares into USD Cash while tightening the remaining 8.4022 shares to an unconditional $453.81 single-close/intraday stop aligns portfolio risk with a 10-distribution-day Downtrend.

book_paragraphs: Welcome back to our institutional underwriting desk. Between our prior November 13 review and the November 20, 2026 market close, Microsoft's footnotes, our 10-year DCF calibration, and the US market tape all shifted meaningfully. This refreshed ten-chapter monograph audits Chapters 1 through 6 blind to price, repairs our audited FY26 unit waterfall to prevent double-counting depreciation, and delivers an exact action plan at $484.52.

On business quality, Microsoft retains its COMPOUNDER_PASS rating with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health. First-quarter revenue climbed 19 percent to $92.3 billion with a 49.7 percent operating margin, Azure surged 48 percent, and commercial backlog reached $677 billion. Yet Pass 1 uncovered heavier cash commitments: $39.4 billion in cash capex, $12.95 billion in component-purchase outflows, and $5.19 billion in new finance leases consumed $57.5 billion of $58.0 billion operating cash flow, prompting a $25.0 billion bond issue on November 4 alongside $364.6 billion in uncommenced leases and $10.0 billion in single-quarter OpenAI revenue.

Modeling that FY27–28 capex hump alongside a 5.04 percent US 10-year Treasury yield (9.1 percent WACC) shows $484.52 already prices in 13.75 percent 10-year revenue growth. Our reconciled Base fair value drops cleanly to $540.00 per share (+11.45 percent upside), flanked by a $375.00 Bear case (-22.6 percent) and a $660.00 Bull case. Inside a Stage 3 pullback (7 distribution days) and a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend, new capital moves to WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT inside $462.00–$476.00 (2.88-to-1 technical R:R; 0.0 percent live allocation).

For your 12.4022 Schwab shares ($6,009.11 value, 8.00 percent weight), we execute TRIM_OVERWEIGHT: sell 4.0 shares (~$1,938.08) to right-size the stake to 8.4022 shares (5.42 percent weight, inside TIER_2 sizing), park 100 percent of trim proceeds in USD cash, and enforce an unconditional intraday or single-close hard stop at $453.81 on the remaining shares.

Notice why pairing TRIM_OVERWEIGHT with an unconditional $453.81 stop matters so much in this environment. When a Stage 3 leader sits inside a ten-distribution-day market Downtrend and offers only 0.51-to-1 fundamental Bear-to-Base skew at $484.52, carrying an oversized 8.00 percent weight behind a slow two-day stop rule leaves your portfolio vulnerable to overnight gap risk. Cutting one-third of the position into cash today while tightening the stop trigger on the remaining 5.42 percent core stake protects capital without surrendering long-term compounding.
Every chapter ahead separates durable fundamental strengths from genuine balance-sheet and concentration risks, giving you a fully reconciled roadmap with exact price and KPI triggers.
